Can we schedule a dedicated-capacity demo/walkthrough that covers: expected throughput for quantized models, burst handling, autoscale behavior, and a brief discussion of routing/fallback policies? Prefer next week in the AM PST.

I'll loop in our infra lead (Sanjay) — he has the detailed traffic matrix.

Ben — thanks. Wed 2026-10-07 10:00 PST works best for us.

Attaching a very short workload summary (metricai_workload_summary.pdf): key points:
- Embeddings (batching): peak burst ~450 QPS, median payload 128 tokens, we batch at client side in groups of 8–16.
- Generations: two endpoints — short replies (~30 tokens) at ~80 r/s and longer synth endpoints (~300 tokens) at 20 r/s.
- We run in us-west-2 and will need predictable egress and option for on-premish VPC peering later.

We prefer a combined session: 25 min sales + 35 min technical deep dive. If possible, can Connor or an infra engineer bring a short note on autoscale warmup and KV-cache behavior under steady QPS? Also, we may need an NDA for the deeper architecture conversation — happy to sign a short one.

Best,
Alex

Alex — great, appreciate the workload summary. Wed 10/07 10:00 PST is blocked on my calendar for you. Proposed plan:

1) 10:00–10:25 Product/fit session (me + Neha): onboarding flow, pricing/commit options for Dedicated, and routing/fallback policies.
2) 10:25–11:00 Technical deep dive (our infra engineer Mina Haddad will join): kernel selection, autoscale warmup, KV cache behavior, quantization tradeoffs for your embedding model, and how we measure 95th pct latency during steady state.

Quick clarifications for Mina to prep:
- Can you confirm your embedding model size (approx params) and whether you plan to use 8-bit quantization?
- Are your client-side batches aggregated into single requests or are you sending multiple concurrent requests per VM?

We can run a short canary during the pilot week if you want to validate a single route at the requested 450 QPS — that would need a short production-equivalent key and a scoped SLA. We can surface the options during the product section.

I'll drop a calendar invite in a separate email with the Zoom link and attach Redwood's standard NDA and a short dedicated one-pager on autoscaling semantics.
